newsitem.title: JORDAN: Israel, Palestinians face new era - Jordan minister.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Palestinians face new era - Jordan minister.

text.p: Jordan's Information Minister Marwan Muasher said on Monday a new era beckoned for Israel and the Palestinians if they could clinch a Jordanian-mediated deal for Palestinian self-rule in the West Bank town of Hebron.
"There is a real chance for a new beginning," Muasher told reporters.

He said an agreement by the Likud-led government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to pull back troops from most of Hebron and make further withdrawals from the West Bank would break with decades of Likud opposition to trading captured Arab land for peace.

"If the Hebron agreement is signed and, more importantly, agreement on redeployment is reached, we will have put the peace process on a new track because this Israeli government will have committed itself to withdrawing from West Bank land, contrary to the old Likud ideology," he said.
Israel and the PLO were discussing final touches to the Hebron deal on Monday and an aide to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat promised an important announcement later.

Muasher, who accompanied Jordan's King Hussein on a mission to Gaza and Tel Aviv on Sunday in a last-ditch effort to rescue talks from the brink of collapse, said the monarch had feared Middle East peace was in "genuine danger".
King Hussein, making his first visit to Gaza, held talks with Arafat before flying to Tel Aviv to see Netanyahu.
"The gap was not big," Muasher said. "But the gap in trust was wide."
